title: committedDebt force-zero in withdrawRewardToken can mask a tiny residual obligation
description: The plan's `withdrawRewardToken` natspec states 'when totalStaked == 0 there are no live claimants and `committedDebt` should already be 0 (no pending accrual). Recompute as defence-in-depth.' The code at line 576 force-zeros `committedDebt`. However, the path that reaches `totalStaked == 0` is not guaranteed to leave `committedDebt == 0`. The `emergencyWithdraw` function (lines 628-651) computes each user's `pending` via two floor divisions: `pending = (amount * accRewardPerShare) / ACC_PRECISION - user.rewardDebt`. The floor truncation can produce a per-user `pending` whose sum (across all users) is at most `committedDebt` (it is bounded by `committedDebt` via the `min` in line 645), but the sum can be strictly LESS than `committedDebt` when accumulated dust truncates downward across multiple users. When the last staker emergency-withdraws, the residual `committedDebt > 0` persists. Subsequently, `withdrawRewardToken` runs with `committedDebt > 0`, but force-sets `committedDebt = 0` at line 576, eliminating an outstanding (tiny) obligation rather than recognising it as part of the balance to sweep. Magnitude: bounded by O(N) wei per claim cycle where N is the number of historical stakers; in practice a handful of wei.
impact: The strong solvency invariant `balance == rewardBudget + committedDebt` is enforced post-sweep by the code, but the pre-sweep state may have had `committedDebt > 0` corresponding to dust the protocol no longer accounts for. There is no actual loss to a live staker because the funds are still present in the contract balance and are sweep-eligible; the issue is purely accounting hygiene. The force-zero masks (rather than reconciles) the dust. Magnitude: O(wei). Not exploitable. Worth tracing only to document the invariant gap.
recommendation: Two options: (a) Add an explicit assertion `require(committedDebt == 0, ...)` to surface any non-zero residual rather than silently zeroing it — this would force the contract to halt and the residue to be investigated; or (b) Document the dust behavior in the natspec ('committedDebt may carry sub-wei dust when totalStaked reaches zero via emergencyWithdraw paths; force-zero accepts this rounding loss to the protocol'). Option (b) matches current intent better and is a one-line comment change. The current natspec ('committedDebt should already be 0') is slightly inaccurate.
attack_scenario: Not an attack vector. The dust residual is a few wei, well below the cost of triggering the path. The finding is purely about the documented invariant not matching what the code can produce in the emergencyWithdraw-only depletion path.
